"'''I Knew I Loved You'''" is a song by Australian [[Pop music|pop]] duo [[Savage Garden]], released through [[Village Roadshow|Roadshow Music]] and [[Columbia Records]] as the second single from their second and final studio album, ''[[Affirmation (Savage Garden album)|Affirmation]]'' (1999). The song was created as an attempt to replicate the composition of Savage Garden's previous single "[[Truly Madly Deeply (song)|Truly Madly Deeply]]". The track was serviced to US [[adult contemporary music|adult contemporary]] and [[contemporary hit radio|top 40]] radio in September 1999 and was issued commercially in Australia on 28 September 1999.

Upon its release, "I Knew I Loved You" topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart for four weeks in early 2000 and topped the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart for 17 weeks, becoming that listing's most successful track of the 2000s decade. The song also reached number one in Canada and Romania and entered the top 10 in Australia, New Zealand, and four European countries. The music video features then teen actress [[Kirsten Dunst]] as [[Darren Hayes]]' love interest. The music video received heavy rotation on [[MTV]].

"I Knew I Loved You" is a song by Australian pop duo Savage Garden, released through Roadshow Music and Columbia Records as the second single from their second and final studio album, Affirmation (1999). The song was created as an attempt to replicate the composition of Savage Garden's previous single "Truly Madly Deeply". The track was serviced to US adult contemporary and top 40 radio in September 1999 and was issued commercially in Australia on 28 September 1999.

Upon its release, "I Knew I Loved You" topped the US Billboard Hot 100 chart for four weeks in early 2000 and topped the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart for 17 weeks, becoming that listing's most successful track of the 2000s decade. The song also reached number one in Canada and Romania and entered the top 10 in Australia, New Zealand, and four European countries. The music video features then teen actress Kirsten Dunst as Darren Hayes' love interest. The music video received heavy rotation on MTV.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Having finished recording material for ''[[Affirmation (Savage Garden album)|Affirmation]]'', Savage Garden members [[Darren Hayes]] and [[Daniel Jones (musician)|Daniel Jones]] were challenged by [[Columbia Records]] executive [[Don Ienner]] to produce the next "[[Truly Madly Deeply (song)|Truly Madly Deeply]]". The duo argued that "Truly Madly Deeply" was a one-of-its-kind song and could not be replicated but also realised that their second album lacked a [[Love song|love ballad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/2194255/the-number-ones-savage-gardens-i-knew-i-loved-you/columns/the-number-ones/|title=The Number Ones: Savage Garden's 'I Knew I Loved You'|last=Breihan|first=Tom|website=[[Stereogum]]|date=1 August 2022|access-date=27 September 2022}}</ref> Hayes and Jones went on to compose "I Knew I Loved You" and submitted it to the record label's executives, who were delighted with the result as they felt it was a strong contender to eclipse the success of "Truly Madly Deeply".

Singer Darren Hayes further explained that the song was born out of a paradoxical situation, being a love song written "in about 40 minutes out of spite towards the record company" at a time when he felt "wounded by love".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/darren-hayes-reflects-on-savage-garden-it-was-an-era-of-glam-excess-and-super-popstars-__13581/ |title = Darren Hayes reflects on 20 years of Savage Garden: Interview| website=[[Official Charts Company|Official Charts]] }}</ref>
sections.text:
Having finished recording material for Affirmation, Savage Garden members Darren Hayes and Daniel Jones were challenged by Columbia Records executive Don Ienner to produce the next "Truly Madly Deeply". The duo argued that "Truly Madly Deeply" was a one-of-its-kind song and could not be replicated but also realised that their second album lacked a love ballad. Hayes and Jones went on to compose "I Knew I Loved You" and submitted it to the record label's executives, who were delighted with the result as they felt it was a strong contender to eclipse the success of "Truly Madly Deeply".

Singer Darren Hayes further explained that the song was born out of a paradoxical situation, being a love song written "in about 40 minutes out of spite towards the record company" at a time when he felt "wounded by love".

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Bill Lamb from [[About.com]] noted "I Knew I Loved You" as a "romantic ballad".<ref>{{cite web|author=Lamb, Bill|url=https://www.liveabout.com/top-pop-songs-2000-3248131|title=Top 100 Pop Songs of 2000|publisher=[[About.com]]|date=11 September 2018|access-date=8 April 2020}}</ref> [[AllMusic]] editor [[Stephen Thomas Erlewine]] called it "hooky and memorable".<ref>{{cite web|first= Stephen Thomas |last= Erlewine |title= Savage Garden - Affirmation |website= [[AllMusic]] |url= https://www.allmusic.com/album/affirmation-mw0000671100 |access-date= 19 April 2020}}</ref> [[Larry Flick]] from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' described the song "as cool and crisp as the autumn air, this simple, direct ballad projects a sweet message of knowing love when you see it." He noted that the song "glides along amid a soft, easy beat, with vocalist Hayes sounding more at ease and confident than ever, like he's singing a timeless classic." He also added that "drenched harmonies add to the overall impact" and called it "absolutely enchanting, one of the most beautiful songs yet of 1999".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1999/BB-1999-09-25.pdf|title=Single Reviews|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=25 September 1999|access-date=10 February 2020|page=24}}</ref> Bob Waliszewski of ''[[Focus on the Family|Plugged In]]'' said that it "describes how it feels to be hopelessly in love".<ref>{{cite web|first= Bob |last= Waliszewski |title= Affirmation |work= Plugged In |publisher= [[Focus on the Family]] |access-date= 27 March 2020 |url= https://www.pluggedin.com/album-reviews/savagegarden-affirmation/}}</ref>
sections.text: Bill Lamb from About.com noted "I Knew I Loved You" as a "romantic ballad". AllMusic editor Stephen Thomas Erlewine called it "hooky and memorable". Larry Flick from Billboard described the song "as cool and crisp as the autumn air, this simple, direct ballad projects a sweet message of knowing love when you see it." He noted that the song "glides along amid a soft, easy beat, with vocalist Hayes sounding more at ease and confident than ever, like he's singing a timeless classic." He also added that "drenched harmonies add to the overall impact" and called it "absolutely enchanting, one of the most beautiful songs yet of 1999". Bob Waliszewski of Plugged In said that it "describes how it feels to be hopelessly in love".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: The song was a success on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], where it spent four weeks at the top, becoming Savage Garden's third and final top-10 hit. It was the last song by an Australian artist to reach the top of the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 for over 12 years, until [[Gotye]] peaked at number one with his single "[[Somebody That I Used to Know]]" in 2012.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/gotyes-somebody-that-i-used-to-know-roars-to-no-1-on-hot-100-1097881/|title=Gotye's 'Somebody That I Used to Know' Roars to No. 1 on Hot 100|last=Trust|first=Gary|magazine=Billboard|date=18 April 2012|access-date=16 March 2025}}</ref> The song remained on the ''Billboard'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart for 124 weeks,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/chart-beat-bonus-80281/|title=Chart Beat Bonus|magazine=Billboard|date=23 March 2001|access-date=8 May 2012}}</ref> breaking the record for 123 weeks set by another of the duo's songs, "Truly Madly Deeply". It ranked number 21 on the all-time Adult Contemporary Chart. The song was certified [[RIAA certification|platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA).
sections.text: The song was a success on the US Billboard Hot 100, where it spent four weeks at the top, becoming Savage Garden's third and final top-10 hit. It was the last song by an Australian artist to reach the top of the Billboard Hot 100 for over 12 years, until Gotye peaked at number one with his single "Somebody That I Used to Know" in 2012. The song remained on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart for 124 weeks, breaking the record for 123 weeks set by another of the duo's songs, "Truly Madly Deeply". It ranked number 21 on the all-time Adult Contemporary Chart. The song was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The accompanying [[music video]] for "I Knew I Loved You" was filmed by director [[Kevin Bray (director)|Kevin Bray]] in August 1999 on a [[New York City Subway]] set that had previously been used on the sitcom ''[[Seinfeld]]''.<ref>[http://www.savagegarden.com/diary/studioupdate6/ Savage Garden diary entry for 26 August 1999] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080919094658/http://www.savagegarden.com/diary/studioupdate6/ |date=19 September 2008 }}</ref> It features Hayes playing out a romantic plot on a subway train, with a female passenger (played by American actress [[Kirsten Dunst]]) as the object of his affections.

At one point, the train comes to a stop due to a [[power outage]]; red emergency lighting comes on and everyone in the carriage joins hands. Hayes, who is sitting opposite his aforementioned love interest, extends his hand to her. As they touch, the video cuts to a [[Montage (filmmaking)|montage]] of the couple walking through a park, bathed in sunlight, laughing and holding hands. The video then cuts back to the carriage as the power comes back on and the train pulls into the station. Hayes and the woman exit with the other passengers, and share a fleeting glance before going their separate ways. Shots of the band performing alone on the subway platform and in the carriage are interspersed throughout the video.
sections.text:
The accompanying music video for "I Knew I Loved You" was filmed by director Kevin Bray in August 1999 on a New York City Subway set that had previously been used on the sitcom Seinfeld. It features Hayes playing out a romantic plot on a subway train, with a female passenger (played by American actress Kirsten Dunst) as the object of his affections.

At one point, the train comes to a stop due to a power outage; red emergency lighting comes on and everyone in the carriage joins hands. Hayes, who is sitting opposite his aforementioned love interest, extends his hand to her. As they touch, the video cuts to a montage of the couple walking through a park, bathed in sunlight, laughing and holding hands. The video then cuts back to the carriage as the power comes back on and the train pulls into the station. Hayes and the woman exit with the other passengers, and share a fleeting glance before going their separate ways. Shots of the band performing alone on the subway platform and in the carriage are interspersed throughout the video.

sections.heading: Cover versions
sections.wikitext: * [[Country music|Country]] singer [[Daryle Singletary]] covered the song for his 2000 album, ''[[Now and Again (Daryle Singletary album)|Now and Again]]''. His version reached number 55 on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Country Songs|Hot Country Singles & Tracks]] chart in October 2000.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Hot Country Singles & Tracks|magazine=Billboard|volume=112|issue=41|page=34|date=7 October 2000}}</ref>
sections.text: * Country singer Daryle Singletary covered the song for his 2000 album, Now and Again. His version reached number 55 on the Billboard Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart in October 2000.
